name: Verdance Minor
geological_features: Low rolling hills of mineral-rich soil
specific_features: Towering fungal canopies reaching extreme heights in the low gravity
Bioluminescent root networks visible through thin topsoil at night
Pollen clouds dense enough to register on atmospheric sensors
description: Verdance Minor is a small terrestrial world blanketed in an extraordinary profusion of plant and fungal life. In the low gravity, vegetation grows to improbable heights -- fungal canopies soar hundreds of meters overhead, and root networks sprawl across entire continents in interconnected webs.

The breathable atmosphere is thick with pollen and spores, giving the air a golden-green haze during peak bloom seasons. The scent is overwhelming: loamy, sweet, and ancient, as though the entire planet were a single immense greenhouse left to run wild.

No fauna has been detected on Verdance Minor, making it one of the rarest known biospheres -- a world where plant life achieved total ecological dominance. Xenobotanists theorize that the low gravity and stable climate created conditions uniquely favorable to flora, while some unknown factor prevented animal evolution entirely.

The planet's rare flora and unique biochemistry represent an invaluable scientific resource. Medicinal compounds derived from Verdance Minor's organisms have shown extraordinary promise in early trials, but the interconnected nature of the root networks means that even limited harvesting could trigger cascading ecological disruption.
